transcript.en: My students built a pulse monitor that showed twelve beats a minute on a healthy volunteer. The circuit was fine. They were sampling a fast signal far too slowly. Today: how a sensor signal becomes numbers, why sampling too slowly invents fake frequencies, and how many bits you really need. An analogue to digital converter measures a voltage at regular instants. The sampling rate is how many measurements per second. Between samples, the converter sees nothing. Shannon's sampling theorem says a signal with no frequencies above B can be rebuilt exactly from samples taken faster than two B per second. Sample slower, and high frequencies fold down as fake low ones. That is aliasing. Mains hum is fifty hertz. Sampled sixty times a second, it appears as a slow ten hertz wave. Sampled at a thousand, it appears correctly as fifty. An n-bit converter splits its range into two to the n levels. A ten-bit converter on three point three volts has steps of about three millivolts. Each extra bit halves the step and adds about six decibels. Students treat sampling as a software setting. Show a spinning wheel under a strobe light, or a film of car wheels turning backwards. They see aliasing before they see the maths. Quick check! A vibration sensor must capture frequencies up to four hundred hertz. What is the lowest sampling rate that can work in theory? Just above eight hundred samples per second. In practice engineers sample several times faster and put an anti-aliasing filter in front of the converter. In the app, open the converter lab. Change the sampling rate and the number of bits, and watch the rebuilt signal improve or fall apart. Your turn. A twelve-bit converter has a reference of four point zero nine six volts. What is the size of one step? One millivolt, because two to the twelve is four thousand and ninety six. Remember: sample faster than twice the highest frequency, filter first, and each bit halves the step. Try it in your next lab: have pairs sample a signal generator at five rates on a microcontroller. They plot what they see and predict each alias before measuring it.

title.en: From a real signal to numbers

body.en:
Shannon’s sampling theorem (1949) states that a signal band-limited to B hertz is determined exactly by samples taken at a rate fs > 2B. If the signal contains energy above fs/2, those components fold back and appear at |f − k × fs|, a false low frequency called an alias. Because aliasing cannot be undone after sampling, practical designs place an analogue anti-aliasing low-pass filter before the converter and sample several times faster than 2B (Lee and Seshia, Introduction to Embedded Systems).

An n-bit converter divides its reference range into 2ⁿ levels, so the step is V_ref/2ⁿ and the quantisation error is uniform within ±½ step. For a full-scale sine wave the signal-to-quantisation-noise ratio is about 6.02n + 1.76 dB. Real converters lose some of that to noise and non-linearity, expressed as the effective number of bits.

Students often treat the sampling rate as a software setting and are surprised when a sensor reports nonsense. Visual analogies, such as a wheel under a strobe or film of wheels that appear to turn backwards, followed by a lab where students predict aliases before measuring them, address that misconception directly.
body.ar:
تنص نظرية المعاينة عند Shannon (١٩٤٩) على أن الإشارة المحدودة النطاق بـ B هرتز تتحدد تمامًا بعينات مأخوذة بمعدّل ⁦fs > 2B⁩. فإذا احتوت الإشارة طاقة فوق ⁦fs/2⁩، ارتدّت تلك المكوّنات وظهرت عند ⁦|f − k × fs|⁩، وهو تردد منخفض زائف يسمى التشويه. ولأن التشويه لا يمكن إزالته بعد المعاينة، تضع التصاميم العملية مرشّحًا تناظريًا منخفض التمرير قبل المحوّل وتعاين أسرع من 2B بعدة مرات (Lee وSeshia، مقدمة في الأنظمة المدمجة).

ويقسّم المحوّل ذو n بت مدى جهده المرجعي إلى 2ⁿ مستوى، فتكون الخطوة ⁦V_ref/2ⁿ⁩ ويكون خطأ التكميم موزعًا بانتظام داخل ±½ خطوة. ولموجة جيبية بكامل المدى تبلغ نسبة الإشارة إلى ضوضاء التكميم نحو ⁦6.02n + 1.76⁩ ديسيبل. وتفقد المحوّلات الحقيقية جزءًا من ذلك بسبب الضوضاء وعدم الخطية، ويُعبّر عن ذلك بعدد البتات الفعلي.

وكثيرًا ما يعامل الطلاب معدّل المعاينة إعدادًا برمجيًا ويُفاجؤون حين يعطي الحسّاس قراءات لا معنى لها. والتشبيهات المرئية، كعجلة تحت ضوء متقطّع أو فيلم لعجلات تبدو كأنها تدور للخلف، يليها معمل يتوقّع فيه الطلاب التشويه قبل قياسه، تعالج هذا التصور الخاطئ مباشرة.

transcript.en: A student team promised a field sensor would run for a year on two AA cells. It died after nine days. The radio was never switched off. Today: how to budget energy with duty cycles, what real-time really means, and how to schedule tasks so deadlines are met. Battery life is capacity divided by average current. A device that sleeps most of the time has an average set by how long and how often it wakes. That fraction is the duty cycle. Awake at twenty milliamps for one second in sixty, and asleep at ten microamps otherwise, the average is about a third of a milliamp. Two thousand milliamp hours then last roughly eight months. In a typical LoRa sensor node, the radio uses most of the energy, even though it is on for a tiny fraction of the time. Sensing and the processor use far less. Real-time does not mean fast. It means every task finishes before its deadline. A hard real-time miss is a failure, like an airbag. A soft miss only lowers quality, like a dropped video frame. Give the shortest period the highest priority. Liu and Layland proved that n periodic tasks always meet their deadlines this way if total utilisation is below n times two to the one over n, minus one. For many tasks that tends to about sixty nine percent. Quick check! A node draws fifty milliamps for one second every hundred seconds and almost nothing otherwise. What is its average current? Half a milliamp: fifty times one in a hundred. So halving the wake time doubles battery life far more cheaply than a bigger battery. In the app, open the battery lab. Change how often the device wakes and how long the radio stays on, and watch the predicted battery life. Your turn. Two tasks: one needs one millisecond every four, the other needs two milliseconds every ten. Is the total utilisation under the rate-monotonic bound for two tasks, about eighty three percent? Yes: a quarter plus a fifth is forty five percent. Remember: battery life follows average current, the radio dominates, and real-time means meeting deadlines. Try it in your next lab: give each team a current meter and their own sensor node. They measure active and sleep current, then predict battery life and defend the number.

body.en:
Battery life is capacity divided by average current. For a node that wakes for a fraction D of the time, I_avg = D × I_active + (1 − D) × I_sleep. Because the radio usually dominates active current, the most effective design levers are fewer and shorter transmissions, aggressive sleep modes, and local processing that sends summaries rather than raw data. Real cells also lose capacity to self-discharge, temperature and high pulse currents, so a measured budget with a safety margin beats a datasheet estimate.

Real-time systems are judged by whether every task meets its deadline, not by average speed. In hard real-time systems a missed deadline is a failure; in soft ones it degrades quality. For independent periodic tasks with deadlines equal to periods, Liu and Layland (1973) proved that rate-monotonic priority assignment (shorter period, higher priority) meets all deadlines if utilisation U = Σ Cᵢ/Tᵢ ≤ n(2^(1/n) − 1), which falls towards ln 2 ≈ 0.69; earliest-deadline-first succeeds for any U ≤ 1.

Students tend to equate real-time with fast and to estimate power from datasheets alone. Labs in which they measure current with a meter or shunt, and timing with a logic analyser or GPIO toggles, replace both misconceptions with evidence.

transcript.en: A cooperative asked us to monitor soil moisture across forty hectares. There is no Wi-Fi, no mains power, and the nearest mobile mast is eight kilometres away. Which network would you choose? Today: how publish and subscribe works, when to use MQTT or CoAP, and the trade-off between range, data rate and energy in LoRa and mesh networks. In MQTT, devices never talk to each other directly. A sensor publishes to a topic on a broker. Any client that subscribed to that topic receives the message. Senders and receivers stay decoupled. MQTT offers three delivery levels. Zero means at most once, with no acknowledgement. One means at least once, so duplicates are possible. Two means exactly once, at the cost of a four-step handshake. Typical ranges in open country: Bluetooth Low Energy tens of metres, Wi-Fi around a hundred, Zigbee mesh a few hundred per hop, and LoRa several kilometres, but at only a few kilobits per second. CoAP, defined in RFC seven two five two, brings a web-like request and response model to tiny devices over UDP. It suits sleepy nodes that are asked for readings, while MQTT suits streams of events. Protocol lectures become lists of acronyms. Instead, give teams a real brief with distance, power and data needs. Make them choose and justify a stack, then test it on hardware. Quick check! A sensor sends a temperature every ten seconds, and an occasional lost reading does not matter. Which MQTT quality of service fits best? Level zero. The next reading arrives in ten seconds, so acknowledgements would only cost energy. Save higher levels for commands, such as opening a valve. In the app, open the mesh lab. Place nodes across a field, remove one, and watch the messages find a new route to the gateway. Your turn. Forty hectares, no power, readings every fifteen minutes, a few bytes each. Which link fits best? LoRa, with one gateway. Remember: publish and subscribe decouples devices, choose the lowest quality of service that is safe, and trade data rate for range. Try it in your next lab: set up a free MQTT broker on a laptop. Each team publishes sensor readings to its own topic, and subscribes to another team's.

body.en:
MQTT (OASIS standard, version 5.0, 2019) is a publish/subscribe protocol over TCP: clients publish messages to hierarchical topics on a broker, which forwards them to subscribers. Decoupling senders from receivers suits event streams and many-to-many data flows. Its three QoS levels trade delivery guarantees (at most once, at least once, exactly once) against messages and energy; retained messages and a last-will message help clients that join late or disconnect unexpectedly.

CoAP (RFC 7252) offers a RESTful request/response model over UDP for constrained devices, with GET, PUT, POST and DELETE on resources, confirmable messages for reliability, and an observe option for push updates. It suits sleepy nodes that are queried for readings and integrates with HTTP through proxies.

The physical link sets the envelope: BLE and Wi-Fi offer high rates over short range; IEEE 802.15.4 meshes such as Zigbee and Thread extend range hop by hop; LoRaWAN reaches kilometres at a few kilobits per second under duty-cycle limits. Atzori, Iera and Morabito (2010) survey these architectures. Teaching with design briefs that specify distance, power and data needs makes students reason about trade-offs instead of memorising acronyms.

MQTT (معيار OASIS، الإصدار 5.0، ٢٠١٩) بروتوكول نشر واشتراك فوق TCP: ينشر العملاء رسائل على مواضيع هرمية لدى وسيط يمرّرها إلى المشتركين. وفصل المرسلين عن المستقبلين يناسب تيارات الأحداث وتدفقات البيانات من كثيرين إلى كثيرين. وتوازن مستويات جودة الخدمة الثلاثة بين ضمانات التسليم (مرة على الأكثر، مرة على الأقل، مرة بالضبط) وعدد الرسائل والطاقة، وتساعد الرسائل المحفوظة ورسالة الوصية العملاء الذين ينضمون متأخرين أو ينقطعون فجأة.

ويقدّم ⁦CoAP (RFC 7252)⁩ نموذج طلب واستجابة على نمط REST فوق UDP للأجهزة المحدودة، مع GET وPUT وPOST وDELETE على الموارد، ورسائل مؤكَّدة للموثوقية، وخيار المراقبة للتحديثات المدفوعة. وهو يناسب العقد النائمة التي تُسأل عن قراءات، ويتكامل مع HTTP عبر الوكلاء.

وتحدد الوصلة المادية الإطار: يقدّم BLE وWi-Fi معدّلات عالية لمدى قصير، وتوسّع الشبكات المتشابكة بمعيار IEEE 802.15.4 مثل Zigbee وThread المدى قفزة بعد قفزة، ويصل LoRaWAN إلى كيلومترات ببضعة كيلوبتات في الثانية في ظل حدود دورة التشغيل. ويستعرض Atzori وIera وMorabito (٢٠١٠) هذه البنى. والتدريس بمهام تصميم تحدد المسافة والطاقة والحاجة إلى البيانات يجعل الطلاب يستدلّون على الموازنات بدل حفظ الاختصارات.

transcript.en: Last year our department bought forty development kits and set a capstone in week one. By week six, half the teams were still debugging their first blinking light. Today: how to sequence hardware labs into a capstone, keep them safe and affordable, and assess teams fairly with a rubric. Scaffolding means structured support that is removed step by step. Early labs give working code and one change to make. Later labs give a goal and a parts list. The capstone gives only a problem. One proven sequence: digital input and output, then sensors and the converter, then timers and interrupts, then low power, then networking. Each lab produces a part the capstone will reuse. Here is a fourteen-week split that worked: eight weeks of scaffolded labs, a week to propose, and five weeks of capstone with a midpoint demo. Keep labs at low voltage, and keep lithium cells charged only on proper chargers. Simulators let students test code before touching hardware, and shared kits with a checkout log keep costs down. A working demo can hide luck. Assess the engineering too: a requirements list, a measured power budget, a test log, and an individual reflection. Peer assessment helps spread marks fairly inside a team. Quick check! Why did half our teams stall in the first six weeks? They faced an open problem before they had the basic skills. The kits were fine. A scaffolded sequence of labs would have built those skills first. In the app, open the board lab. Wire a sensor and an output on a virtual board, and run it before anyone touches real hardware. Your turn. In a team of four, one student did almost nothing. Which evidence best supports adjusting individual marks? Structured peer assessment with the commit and test logs. Remember: scaffold before the capstone, keep labs safe and cheap, and assess the engineering as well as the demo. Try it this term: list the skills your capstone needs. Then check that an earlier lab teaches each one, and add a lab for any skill that is missing.

body.en:
Open-ended hardware projects motivate students, but novices facing an unstructured problem spend their time on configuration and debugging rather than learning. Scaffolding, structured support faded over time, resolves this: early labs supply working code and ask for one modification; later labs supply a goal and a parts list; the capstone supplies only a problem. A sequence of GPIO, sensors and ADC, timers and interrupts, low power and networking produces components the capstone reuses (Lee and Seshia describe a similar progression).

Safety and cost are design constraints. Keep circuits at low voltage, charge lithium cells only with suitable chargers, require a short safety briefing, and use simulators so code is tested before hardware. Shared kits with a checkout log, and a small stock of spares, make a lab sustainable on a modest budget.

A working demo can conceal luck or one student’s effort. Assess the engineering evidence: a requirements list, a measured power budget, a test log, version-control history, and an individual reflection. Structured peer assessment adjusts individual marks within teams. Constructive alignment (Biggs and Tang) ties each of these to a stated outcome, and an analytic rubric shared at the start tells teams what quality looks like.

تحفّز مشاريع الأجهزة المفتوحة الطلاب، لكن المبتدئين أمام مشكلة غير منظّمة يقضون وقتهم في الإعداد وإصلاح الأخطاء بدل التعلّم. ويحلّ ذلك التدرّج، أي الدعم المنظّم الذي يُسحب مع الوقت: تقدّم المعامل الأولى كودًا يعمل وتطلب تعديلًا واحدًا، وتقدّم المعامل اللاحقة هدفًا وقائمة قطع، ولا يقدّم مشروع التخرّج إلا مشكلة. وينتج تسلسل من منافذ الدخل والخرج، فالحسّاسات والمحوّل، فالمؤقتات والمقاطعات، فالطاقة المنخفضة، فالشبكات، مكوّنات يعيد المشروع استخدامها (ويصف Lee وSeshia تدرّجًا مشابهًا).

والسلامة والتكلفة قيود تصميم. أبقِ الدوائر على جهد منخفض، واشحن خلايا الليثيوم بشواحن مناسبة فقط، واشترط إحاطة قصيرة بالسلامة، واستخدم المحاكيات لاختبار الكود قبل الأجهزة. وتجعل العُدد المشتركة بسجل استلام، ومخزون صغير من القطع الاحتياطية، المعمل مستدامًا بميزانية متواضعة.

وقد يخفي العرض العامل حظًا أو جهد طالب واحد. فقيّم الأدلة الهندسية: قائمة المتطلبات، وميزانية طاقة مقيسة، وسجل الاختبارات، وتاريخ التحكم في النسخ، وتأملًا فرديًا. ويعدّل تقييم الأقران المنظّم الدرجات الفردية داخل الفرق. ويربط التنسيق البنّاء (Biggs وTang) كلًّا من ذلك بناتج معلن، ويخبر معيار التقييم التحليلي المُشارك منذ البداية الفرقَ بشكل الجودة المطلوبة.
